correctness.rationale: Cauchy projection formula gives surface estimator ratio as the surface-area-measure mean of 2q(v), q=sum w_i|u_i dot v|. The primary source sharp defect theorem, independently reproduced using Minkowski surface-area existence for approximate antipodal masses, proves E=max_v|2q(v)-1| over all full-dimensional bodies. For each i choose a normal orthogonal to the other two directions, forcing q<=w_i; since sum weights=1, min q<=1/3 and E>=1/3. Equal-weight orthogonal triples give q in [1/3,1/sqrt(3)], so E=1/3. Equality for arbitrary triples forces all w_i>=1/3 and w_i|u_i dot v_i|>=1/3, hence all weights 1/3 and pairwise perpendicular directions. If E<=1/3+eps<1, then q>=L=1/3-eps/2, implying w_i in [L,1-2L] and |u_i dot v_i|>=L/(1/3+eps); orthogonal decomposition gives the explicit 3 sqrt(eps(4+3eps))/(2(1+3eps)) angle bound. The exact orthogonal weight family yields E=1/3+delta and saturates both weight inequalities; the tilt family has qmin=cos(theta)/3, qmax=sqrt(3+2sin(theta))/3, hence E=1-2cos(theta)/3 for theta<=pi/6, proving sharp square-root exponent. Every quantifier is over calibrated positive triples and full-dimensional convex bodies, and no computation is used as an infinite-dimensional proof.

originality.rationale: The numerical 1/3 worst error for a fixed orthogonal three-direction cubature is already covered by the 2009 Kiderlen--Meschenmoser paper, and is explicitly credited. The new claim is the global three-view optimization with a unique optimizer even when weights and directions vary, plus explicit weight and angle stability with optimal orders. Full-text checks of the 2026 directional-kernel source, the closely relevant 2009 finite Crofton estimator source, and the 2023 spherical minimax design source found no published statement or stronger implication covering this whole claim. Alias searches of the published findings index and mathematical literature did not locate an equivalent three-view two-sided stability theorem.
residual_risks: The 2009 general zonotope bound contains a strong premise and the orthogonal numerical 1/3 case; the optimization/uniqueness and stability arguments are short, so an unindexed follow-up could have included them.
Fu--Wang--Yan 2023 give an orthogonal optimizer for a related one-sided absolute-dot-product objective; this is not a proof of the calibrated two-sided near-rigidity statement.
Some digital-stereology literature predating 2009 is indexed mostly through abstracts rather than complete theorem texts and might contain an equivalent three-view design observation.
The angular stability coefficient is not proved sharp; only its square-root exponent is.

value.rationale: The cited 2026 work proves finite Cauchy quadrature cannot be universally exact and quantifies error using a continuous spherical potential, naturally raising the exact optimal small-node design problem. The three-view case is the smallest full-dimensional sampling budget for 3D projection-area estimation, and its sharp global optimizer and unique equality case matter for choosing measurement directions. Unlike merely recomputing the known 1/3 error for a coordinate rule, the theorem rules out every oblique or unequally weighted competitor and gives explicit robust error-to-design guarantees. Sharp order of weight and angular deviations is established by distinct constructive perturbations, showing the estimate detects a true second-order geometric boundary rather than a cosmetic reformulation.
